page: Vultr vhp-2c-4gb-intel is a virtual server instance belonging to the High Performance family. It features an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor configured with 2 shared vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with Hyper-Threading running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with a 100 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this system.

Benchmark data indicates moderate single-core capabilities alongside constrained multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves average single-core performance in stress-ng (1464.88) and single-threaded compression tests, such as gzip (24.52 GB/sec) and bzip3 (9.46 GB/sec). However, multi-core and memory-bound metrics fall into lower percentiles. The Geekbench multi-core score of 1966.0 and the Passmark database operations score of 683.09 are in the bottom 10% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with large-block read-only bandwidth recorded at 18.34 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 14.91 GB/sec.

Due to the shared CPU allocation, this instance exhibits a performance-to-resource tradeoff, where single-threaded tasks perform adequately but concurrent or memory-intensive operations face bottlenecks. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of 100 GB of NVMe SSD storage alongside a low-resource shared CPU profile makes it a budget-friendly option for entry-level workloads. It is suited for lightweight applications such as basic static web serving, simple Redis key-value operations, and small-scale development or testing environments that do not require sustained multi-core execution.
